addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	package markdown
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/yuin/goldmark"
8		gast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
9		"github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension"
10		east "github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension/ast"
11		"github.com/yuin/goldmark/parser"
12		"github.com/yuin/goldmark/text"
13	
14		mast "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/ast"
15		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/extensions"
16		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/renderer"
17		storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
18	)
19	
20	// ExtractedData contains all metadata extracted from markdown in a single pass.
21	type ExtractedData struct {
22		Tags     []string
23		Mentions []string
24		Property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property
25	}
26	
27	// Service handles markdown metadata extraction.
28	// It uses goldmark to parse markdown and extract tags, properties, and snippets.
29	// HTML rendering is primarily done on frontend using markdown-it, but backend provides
30	// RenderHTML for RSS feeds and other server-side rendering needs.
31	type Service interface {
32		// ExtractAll extracts tags, properties, and references in a single parse (most efficient)
33		ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
34	
35		// ExtractTags returns all #tags found in content
36		ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
37	
38		// ExtractProperties computes boolean properties
39		ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
40	
41		// RenderMarkdown renders goldmark AST back to markdown text
42		RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)
43	
44		// RenderHTML renders markdown content to HTML
45		RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
46	
47		// GenerateSnippet creates plain text summary
48		GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
49	
50		// ValidateContent checks for syntax errors
51		ValidateContent(content []byte) error
52	
53		// RenameTag renames all occurrences of oldTag to newTag in content
54		RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
55	}
56	
57	// service implements the Service interface.
58	type service struct {
59		md goldmark.Markdown
60	}
61	
62	// Option configures the markdown service.
63	type Option func(*config)
64	
65	type config struct {
66		enableTags     bool
67		enableMentions bool
68	}
69	
70	// WithTagExtension enables #tag parsing.
71	func WithTagExtension() Option {
72		return func(c *config) {
73			c.enableTags = true
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// WithMentionExtension enables @mention parsing.
78	func WithMentionExtension() Option {
79		return func(c *config) {
80			c.enableMentions = true
81		}
82	}
83	
84	// NewService creates a new markdown service with the given options.
85	func NewService(opts ...Option) Service {
86		cfg := &config{}
87		for _, opt := range opts {
88			opt(cfg)
89		}
90	
91		exts := []goldmark.Extender{
92			extension.GFM, // GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks)
93		}
94	
95		// Add custom extensions based on config
96		if cfg.enableTags {
97			exts = append(exts, extensions.TagExtension)
98		}
99		if cfg.enableMentions {
100			exts = append(exts, extensions.MentionExtension)
101		}
102	
103		md := goldmark.New(
104			goldmark.WithExtensions(exts...),
105			goldmark.WithParserOptions(
106				parser.WithAutoHeadingID(), // Generate heading IDs
107			),
108		)
109	
110		return &service{
111			md: md,
112		}
113	}
114	
115	// parse is an internal helper to parse content into AST.

I have what I need.

**h14.**

**Computation site.** `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88`, which delegates the actual work to the goldmark-based markdown service: `(*service).ExtractAll` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-422` (a single AST parse + walk). `RebuildMemoPayload` writes only `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (runner.go:85-86); user-set fields like `Payload.Location` are left alone and assigned separately (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:111-113`). The stored shape is `MemoPayload.Property`, documented in `proto/store/memo.proto:14-22` as "The calculated properties from the memo content."

**Triggers.**
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, on every memo creation (after the content-length check, before `Store.CreateMemo`).
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, only inside the `path == "content"` branch of the update mask; the recomputed payload is written along with the new content (`update.Payload = memo.Payload`, line 452). Updating visibility, pinned state, etc. does not recompute.
- A batch backfill path exists: `Runner.RunOnce` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72` re-runs `RebuildMemoPayload` over all memos in batches of 100. Note it is currently not wired up anywhere — `grep` for `memopayload.` finds only the two `memo_service.go` call sites, so nothing constructs this runner today.

**Extracted properties.** From `ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:376-408`):
- `Tags` — `#tag` nodes, skipping tags nested inside links/images (`asMemoTagNode`, markdown.go:134-140), deduplicated preserving original case (line 418).
- `Property.Title` — text of the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading (lines 384-389, via `extractHeadingText`).
- `Property.HasLink` — any `KindLink` node.
- `Property.HasCode` — any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span.
- `Property.HasTaskList` — any GFM task checkbox.
- `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` — any task checkbox with `IsChecked == false`.

`ExtractAll` also collects `Mentions` (lowercased `@username` nodes, line 379-381), but `RebuildMemoPayload` discards them — they are not part of the persisted payload.

**Consumers (the "lists/previews" use).** `Property` is converted to the API type in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:49,315` and aggregated in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:141-152,257-268`; it is also filterable in the store (`store/test/memo_filter_test.go:523-610`). Separately and *not* stored, the list/preview `snippet` is generated on the fly at conversion time by `GenerateSnippet` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:264-346`) via `getMemoContentSnippet` (`memo_service_converter.go:76-80`, `memo_relation_service.go:154-173`, `user_service_notifications.go:318-323`).
